severity_criteria.source_excerpt: 5.1 Inclusion Criteria: "Participants are eligible to be included in the study only if all of the following criteria apply:" "IGA score of 2 to 3 at the screening and baseline visits." "%BSA (excluding the scalp) with AD involvement of 3% to 20% at the screening and" "baseline visits." "For children aged 6 years to < 12 years, baseline itch NRS score ≥ 4 (see Section 8.2.7)." "4." "5." "6." -- IGA 2 to 3 and affected BSA 3% to 20% are baseline severity eligibility thresholds. The separate itch NRS threshold of at least 4 applies only to children aged 6 to under 12 and is not represented as a population-wide criterion; the protocol does not literally call eligibility moderate_to_severe.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 6.6 Concomitant Medications and Procedures, 6.6.1-6.6.3: "The following are permitted during the study:" "• Participants may use bland emollients (except those containing urea, salicylic acid, or" "throughout the course of the study." "• Participants may use nonsedating, over-the-counter antihistamines." "• Participants may continue using sedating antihistaminic drugs as long as their use is" "part of a preexisting and well-established regimen." "• Allergen immunotherapy (desensitization) that is ongoing at a stable dose at the time" "of study entry may be continued while on study but only at the same dose." "6.6.3." "The following are not permitted during the study:" "• Topical corticosteroids, tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, and PDE4-inhibitors (Eucrisa)." "• Other topical agents for AD (except bland emollients as noted in Section 6.6.1)." "• Treatment known to affect the course of AD." "• Systemic corticosteroids (except the example stated in Section 6.6.2), methotrexate," "cyclosporin A, azathioprine and biologic therapies, or other immunosuppressant" "agents." "• Phototherapy or tanning beds." -- The restrictions and permissions listed are during-study policies. The protocol also requires agreement to stop AD-treatment agents from screening through final safety follow-up, but it does not establish a named background regimen.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 3.2 Control of Type I Error: "NCT Number: NCT04921969" "For the primary and key secondary analyses, an overall 2-sided Type I error of 0.05 will be used." "A graphical procedure with gatekeeping testing strategy for the primary and key secondary" "analyses will be implemented." "The underlying procedure is derived using the methodology" "developed by Bretz et al (2009)." "The method will guarantee a strong control of the family-wise" "error rate." "In Step 1, 2 families of 4 elementary hypotheses tests at Week 8 are grouped according to" "• Family 1 (1.5% BID vs vehicle):" "− H11: proportion of participants who achieve IGA-TS" "− H12: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "• Family 2 (0.75% BID vs vehicle):" "− H21: proportion of participants who achieve IGA-TS" "− H22: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "Step 2 has 2 families of 4 hypotheses tests:" "• Family 3 (1.5% BID vs vehicle and 0.75% BID vs vehicle on Day 7 Itch NRS):" "− H13: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 7 (Week 1) between 1.5% BID and vehicle" "− H23: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 7 (Week 1) between 0.75% BID and vehicle" "• Family 4 (1.5% BID vs vehicle and 0.75% BID vs vehicle on Day 3 Itch NRS):" "− H14: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 3 between 1.5% BID and vehicle" "− H24: proportion of participants with a ≥ 4-grade improvement in Itch NRS score" "over baseline to Day 3 between 0.75% BID and vehicle" "To control the overall Type I error rate, 2-sided α = 0.05, the Bonferroni's method will be used." "In Step 1, within Family 1 and 2, the endpoints are tested in a fixed sequence at a Bonferronized" "2-sided α = 0.025 level." "The key secondary endpoint will be tested only if the associated primary" "endpoint is rejected." "For any treatment strength, if the 2 related null hypotheses can be rejected," "then the fixed sequence for the other treatment strength can be conducted at the 2-sided α = 0.05" "If all null hypotheses in Family 1 and 2 are rejected, in Step 2, the endpoints in Family 3" "(H13 and H23) will be tested using Bonferroni-Hochberg's procedure with overall 2-sided" "α = 0.05 level." "If both hypotheses in Family 3 are rejected, the endpoints in Family 4 (H14 and" "H24) will be tested similarly using Bonferroni-Hochberg's procedure with overall 2-sided" "α = 0.05 level." -- The SAP describes a graphical gatekeeping strategy with strong familywise control at overall two-sided alpha 0.05. Family 1 and 2 test Week 8 IGA-TS then the associated key secondary endpoint at alpha 0.025, with the stated conditional continuation across strengths; only after both families reject does Step 2 test Family 3, then Family 4 if Family 3 rejects. The schema has no enum for the complete graphical procedure; alpha_split records the described families and testing methods, while testing_sequence remains empty because the plan has conditional fixed-sequence and gatekeeping branches. The SAP is dated but does not explicitly state it was finalized.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Protocol Summary, Table 2 Key Study Design Elements, Tables 3-4 Schedule of Activities: "Table 2: Key Study Design Elements" "Study Design Randomized (2:2:1), double-blind, VC period (8 weeks) followed by" "an LTS period (44 weeks) and a 30-day safety follow-up period after" "the last application of study cream." "Estimated Duration of Study Screening period: up to 28 (+ 7) days" "Participation VC period: approximately 8 weeks" "LTS period: approximately 44 weeks" "Safety follow-up period: 30 days after the last application of study" "treatment or last study visit" "Total: up to approximately 61 weeks" "inclusion criteria during the screening period (up to 28 days or up to 35 days for participants" "taking prior medications that require a 4-week washout period [see Section 5.2, Exclusion" "Table 3: Schedule of Activities: Vehicle-Controlled Period" "Screening VC Period" "Days −28 Day 1/ Wk 2 Wk 4 Wk 8b/ET" "Visit Day (Range) (+ 7a) to −1 Baseline (± 3 d) (± 3 d) (± 3 d) Notes and Protocol Section" "a For prior medications that require a 4-week washout period (see Section 5.2, Exclusion Criterion 6b), a 35-day screening period is allowed." "Table 4: Schedule of Activities: Long-Term Safety Period" "LTS Period Safety Follow-Up" "Wk 16, Wk 28, Wk 40, Wk 52/ 30 (+ 7) Days After" "Wk 12 20, and 24 32, and 36 44, and 48 EOT/ET Unscheduled Last Study Cream" "Visit Day (Range) (± 7 d) (± 7 d) (± 7 d) (± 7 d) (± 7 d) Visit Applicationa Notes and Protocol Section" "Following the end of treatment (Week 52/EOT or ET), all participants will have a safety" "follow-up visit 30 days later (or 30 days after the last application of study treatment if the" "Week 52/EOT or ET visit was not performed)." "Apply study cream at site X X X X Section 6.1; only for participants with active" -- The protocol has a full per-visit Schedule of Activities (Tables 3-4). Screening is up to 28 days, with 35 days allowed for the specified prior-medication washout; this is not a routine screening washout. Treatment is Week 1-8 followed by LTS Week 8-52; safety follow-up is 30 days after the last application (or EOT/ET when applicable). The protocol estimates total participation up to approximately 61 weeks. LTS visits occur at Week 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48 and 52; Week 1 and Day 3 key secondary assessments are diary-based, not added as clinic visits.

value.applies_to_period: Vehicle-controlled and long-term safety treatment periods
value.rationale: The protocol prohibits other topical AD treatments and treatments known to affect AD during study treatment; worsening AD requiring a prohibited concomitant medication requires study-cream discontinuation. Bland emollients are permitted, so this represents prohibited AD rescue treatment rather than a prohibition on all supportive care.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 6.6.1-6.6.3 Permitted, Restricted, and Prohibited Medications; 6.5.2 discontinuation criteria: "The following are permitted during the study:" "• Participants may use bland emollients (except those containing urea, salicylic acid, or" "• Other topical agents for AD (except bland emollients as noted in Section 6.6.1)." "• Treatment known to affect the course of AD." "Participants must be discontinued from study treatment for the following reasons:" "• AD worsens during either the VC period or the LTS period, to the point where the" "extent of AD to be treated (ie." "all areas excluding the scalp) exceeds 20% BSA." "The following are not permitted during the study:" "• Topical corticosteroids, tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, and PDE4-inhibitors (Eucrisa)." "• Systemic corticosteroids (except the example stated in Section 6.6.2), methotrexate," "cyclosporin A, azathioprine and biologic therapies, or other immunosuppressant" "agents." -- There is no permitted rescue regimen or rescue trigger; the protocol explicitly prohibits alternative AD treatments during study treatment, with bland emollients allowed. The treatment policy applies through the Week 52 treatment period; follow-up is a safety observation period.

published_results.source_excerpt: 14.1 Atopic Dermatitis, Table 5: "52.2% (84/161) 15.4% (12/78) 36.7% (25.5%, 48.0%) 50.7% (74/146) 16.3% (13/80) 35.8% (24.4%, 47.2%) Pediatric Subjects 2 to 11 Years of Age A double-blind, randomized, vehicle-controlled trial, TRuE-AD3 (NCT04921969), enrolled a total of 330 pediatric subjects, 2 to 11 years of age, and subjects were treated twice daily (BID) for 8 weeks." "The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects at Week 8 achieving IGA treatment success (IGA-TS) defined as a score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with ≥ 2 grade improvement from baseline." "Efficacy results for OPZELURA from TRuE-AD3 are summarized in Table 5." "Table 5: Efficacy Results at Week 8 in Pediatric Subjects 2 to 11 Years of Age with Atopic Dermatitis (TRuE-AD3) OPZELURA (N = 131) Vehicle (N = 65) Treatment Difference and 95% Confidence Interval IGA-TS Defined as an IGA score of 0 or 1 with a ≥ 2-grade improvement from baseline." "56.5% 10.8% 45.7% (34.7%, 56.8%) 14.2 Nonsegmental Vitiligo Two double-blind, randomized, vehicle-controlled trials of identical design (TRuE‑V1 and TRuE‑V2, NCT04052425 and NCT04057573, respectively) enrolled a total of 674 adult and pediatric subjects aged 12 years and older (11% of subjects were 12 to 17 years of age and 7% were 65 years or older)." -- TRuE-AD3 is explicitly identified with NCT04921969 and the label defines its Week 8 primary IGA-TS endpoint. Table 5's OPZELURA N=131 and Vehicle N=65 columns provide the arm denominators and printed rates. The OPZELURA arm maps to base arm OG002#full_analysis_set (the 131-participant 1.5% arm); vehicle maps to OG000#full_analysis_set. The table reports rates but not responder counts, so responders remain null. The treatment-difference confidence interval is not an arm-level interval and is not copied into these rows.
